interest: This document provides a concise administrative window into U.S. wartime counterintelligence anxieties in neutral Turkey during World War II. Although it consists solely of a jacket case cover list indexing a single memorandum from Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, it highlights high-level Washington concern over the vulnerability of the American Embassy in Ankara to Japanese espionage networks. It is also valuable for researchers tracing State Department decimal filing practices and cross-references regarding Axis intelligence and subversive activities in the Middle East.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers for Jacket Case' under decimal file 894.20267, titled 'Alleged Japanese subversive activities in Turkey' for the year 1944. The jacket sheet logs a single item dated January 11, 1944, from Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. ('State Dept. A-B (Berle)'), warning that the American Embassy at Ankara was vulnerable to Japanese intelligence agents and urging that defensive measures be undertaken for its protection, with a cross-reference noted to file 124.675.

subfiles.about: A State Department jacket case sheet indexing an entry on the vulnerability of the American Embassy in Ankara to Japanese espionage agents.
subfiles.from: Adolf A. Berle, Jr. (State Dept. A-B)
subfiles.summary: This document serves as the docket index sheet for jacket case 894.20267 regarding alleged Japanese subversive activities in Turkey in 1944. It records a single paper dated January 11, 1944, originating from Assistant Secretary of State Adolf A. Berle, Jr. The entry notes that the American Embassy at Ankara is vulnerable to Japanese agents and urges that someone begin working to protect the mission, referencing file number 124.675.
